en.html:
This section draws heavily on the lists provided by “Harumaki” and “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki”. I would like to take this opportunity to express my gratitude. There are more collections of tales and military chronicles than primary sources. Many are available online via the National Diet Library's Modern Digital Library. Listed in Japanese alphabetical order.

Aioi-shu

Included in the middle volume of the Iwaki Historical Materials Series

Aizu Ashina-ki

From the origins to the downfall of the Ashina clan. Included in Sendai Sosho, Vol. 5.

Aizu Shika Goko

Mukai Shinbei Yoshishige, Kanbun 2 (1662). Included in the Modern Digital Library. For a modern Japanese translation, see “The Era of the Aizu Shika Goko”.

Aizu Kassenki

I have received a copy of the historical document. It is published in "Aizu Shiryo Sosho Vol. 3" and is included in the Modern Digital Library. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > Aizu no Sen'eki > Aizu Kassenki”.

Ashitate Family Documents

Record of the Ayugai Family of the Sendai Date Clan

Ihoku Gunki

Includes Masamune's campaign in Oku-Aizu. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > Aizu Campaigns”.

Inan Gunki

Includes Masamune's campaign in Oku-Aizu. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > Aizu Campaigns”.

Inan Kassenki

Includes Masamune's campaign in Oku-Aizu. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > Aizu Campaigns”.

Goka Nenpyoroku

A chronology of the Ichinoseki Tamura family, from the first generation, Muneyoshi, to the fifth generation, Murataka.

Ou Eikei Gunki

Published by Jinbutsu Orai-sha. A military chronicle written in clear, accessible prose. It has been reprinted.

The Military Tale of Aizu Hibara in Oshu

The Rise and Fall of the Anazawa Clan. Includes Masamune's Battle of Hibara. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > Aizu Campaigns”. Included in the Aizu Materials Series. Available at the Modern Digital Library.

Oshu Kasai-ki

Included in Iwate Prefecture Sengoku Period Documents II

Oshu Kasai Jikki

Compiled by Masanobu Kasai, second son of Harunobu Kasai, in Bunroku 2. Included in Shintei Zoho Shiseki Shuran, Sequel 8.

Okuso Chawaki

A tale of Soma. Included in the second volume of the Iwaki Historical Materials Collection.

Onko Chishinki

Events in the Aizu-Inan region from Tensho 17 to Genroku are listed in bullet points. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > Aizu Campaigns”.

Kasai-Osaki Seisui-ki

The Rise and Fall of the Kasai and Osaki Clans. Included in Sendai Sosho, Vol. 7.

Katakura Daidai-ki

Included in the History of Shiroishi City.

Kimura Uemon Memorandum

Published by Shinjinbutsu Orai-sha as Records of the Words and Deeds of Masamune Date: Kimura Uemon Memorandum. Masamune's first-person narrative is particularly intriguing. Shigezane also appears.

Excerpts from the Records of Great-Great-Grandfather Terumune, Great-Grandfather Masamune, and Grandfather Tadamune

Kodan Fudenjo

Onagoshu

A record of Masamune's words and deeds. Included in Volume 1 of the Sendai Sosho. An affordable edition, recompiled by Tomio Takahashi from Hobundo, titled "Date Masamune Genkoroku — Masamune-ko Meigoshu" (http://www.amazon.co.jp/exec/obidos/ASIN/4832301950/oysannohitori-22), is now available.

Chawaki Isetsu Kaisenshu

A lost entry from the Okuso Chawaki. Included in the second volume of the Iwaki Historical Materials Series.

Shigezane-ki

Written by Shigezane Date. A military chronicle spanning from Tensho 12 to Keicho 5. Included in Volume 3 of the Sendai Sosho.

Jozan Kidan

A collection of tales of military prowess.

Jinkai-shu

Included in “A Study of the Date-ke Jinkai-shu”. Laws of the Date clan.

Shinpen Togoku-ki

The rise and fall of the various eastern powers such as the Satake, Ashina, Date, Iwaki, and Mogami. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > The Aizu Campaigns”.

Shintatsu Ittoshi

Included in Iwaki Shiryo Sosho, Vol. 1

Izumi Tadaki

Includes Masamune's campaign in Oku-Aizu. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > Aizu Campaigns”.

Section on Treasures: Register of Sendai Family Swords (Sendai Family Sword Registry; Record of the Lineage of the Date Family Treasure Swords)

Available for viewing on the Tokyo National Museum Digital Archive.

Sendai Kojoki

An introduction to the ancient castles of the Sendai domain. Included in Volume 4 of the Sendai Sosho.

Sendai Shikan

By Kenzo Yano. May 1900

Sendai Shiryo

1892, Senjin Oka. Biographies of figures from the early Sendai Domain. It's debatable whether this qualifies as a historical source, but I'll include it here anyway.

Sendai Shiden

By Shozo Suzuki. Dec. 1892.

Biographical History of Sendai

Written by Toraiwa Dosetsu, compiled by Kiyoaki Nami and edited by Bunsuke Ashitate. Sendai Bunko Series, Vol. 4, Meiji 29.1

Record of Retainers of the Sendai Domain

Biographies of Figures of the Sendai Domain

Miyagi Prefecture. 1908

Sendai Domain Founders' Records

Written by Takedo (Kaoru) Saito, Seiundo, Nov. 1881

Historical Records of the Founders of the Sendai Domain

Edited by Shuji Shimo-Iizaka and Eiji Tanno, Meiji 17.8

Deeds of the Founder of the Sendai Domain in Honor of the Emperor

Written by Kenzo Yano, May 1899

Sendai Bukan

Written by Nobuyoshi Sato. A biography of Masamune. Included in Volume 3 of the Sendai Sosho supplement.

Registers of Officials of Sendai Domain

The stipends of the Sendai domain retainers are listed in alphabetical order. Included in Volume 6 of the Sendai Sosho.

Sendoki

A military chronicle of the Sendo region centered on Masamune. Included in the Battles section of Volume 22, Part 2 of the Zoku Gunsho Ruiju.

Date-ke Kyuki

A transcribed copy is held at the Historiographical Institute of the University of Tokyo.

Records of the Date Family Administration

The official history of the Date clan. Seizan (Terumune) is included in the Jinbutsu Orai-sha Sengoku Shiryo Sosho "Date Shiryo-shu". There are also volumes covering two generations: Seizan (Terumune) and Teizan (Masamune). The complete set was published by Hobundo. As the administrator living in the Kansai region, I scrambled to find a library that possessed this set and was willing to lend it.

Date-ke Seshin Kafu

Genealogical records and family rosters of the Date clan, included in the subsequent volumes of the Sendai Sosho

Supplement to the Genealogy of the Date Clan Retainers

Included in the Sendai Series subsequent volumes

Brief Genealogy of the Date Clan

Written by Kibun Tanabe et al., Meiji 29.9 (Sendai Bunko Series; Vol. 7)

Biographies of the Date Clan Retainers

Written by Kibun Tanabe, edited by Shozo Suzuki, Sendai Sosho, Vol. 7, Sendai Sosho Publishing Association, June 1914.

Date-ke Seshinroku

Written by Hirotada Sazawa, Koun Seisha, Meiji 38

Diary of Shigezane Date

Included in the Gunsho Ruiju, Battles section. Nearly identical to the Shigezane-ki. A landmark historical document—the first "historical source" the administrator ever encountered. It was in the high school library.

Date Clan Genealogical Record

Study on the Genealogical Lineage of the Date Clan

Compiled by Tsunamura Date: The Official History of the Date Clan, Part 1. Sendai Bunko Series, Vol. 9

Study of the Genealogical Lineage of the Date Clan

Compiled by Tsunamura Date, edited by Bunsuke Ashitate and Kiyoaki Sakanami. Included in the Sendai Bunko Series, Vol. 10, and the Jinbutsu Orai-sha Sengoku Historical Materials Series ["Date Historical Materials Collection" (#/post/shigezane/rekishi-shiryou-index)]. The official history of the Date clan prior to Harumune.

Brief Record of the Date Clan Genealogy

Written by Kibun Tanabe, supplemented by Kisei Tanabe, and further expanded by Kiyoaki Sakanami, Sept. 1894, Sendai Bunko Series, Vol. 7

Diary of Terumune Date

Diaries from around Terumune's circle in Tensho 2. Included in "Date Family Documents" and "History of Fukushima Prefecture, Vol. 7."

Date Tensho Diary

Included in the Jinbutsu Orai-sha Sengoku Historical Materials Series "Date Historical Materials Collection". It's interesting that the weather is recorded.

Date Hikan

A military chronicle of Ou centered on the Date clan. Included in Volumes 17 and 18 of the Sendai Sosho. I wonder how much of it can be trusted.

Date Benranshi

Written by Dogan Sakuma. Covers the period from Asamune to Tsunamura. Included in Volume 3 of the Sendai Sosho.

Record of the Posthumous Memoirs of Taketoku Date

Written by Tomonao Hori. Article on Masamune. Included in Sendai Sosho, Vol. 10.

Collected Poems of Lord Masamune Date

Included in Volume 1 of the Sendai Sosho. A collection of poems by Masamune.

Historical Materials on the Biography of Lord Masamune Date

A wonderful book that compiles various historical materials in chronological order to chronicle Masamune's life. I found this one at a secondhand bookstore in Sanjo Kawaramachi, Kyoto. It was deeply moving to realize that there are others in the Kansai region who own it as well.

Chronology of Lord Masamune Date

Written by Dogan Sakuma. A chronology of Masamune. Included in Sendai Sosho, Vol. 1.

Date Ryakukei

Written by Kiyoaki Sakunami. Included in Vol. 1 of the Sendai Sosho, Sendai Bunko Sosho, Vol. 1.

Tamura Hyosenki

Included in the second volume of the Iwaki Historical Materials Collection

Too Gunki

Included in the Battles section of Volume 22, Part 2 of the Zoku Gunsho Ruiju. Focuses on the Nanbu clan. Also contains entries on the Waga Uprising.

Too Roko Monogatari

Accounts of Sendai Castle and military affairs. Included in Volume 8 of the Sendai Sosho.

Togoku Taiheiki

A military chronicle held by the Tanno family, retainers of the Watari Date clan. While the term "Togoku Taiheiki" generally refers to the work depicting the so-called "Sekigahara of the North," this volume begins with Terumune's campaign against Igu in Tensho 10 and concludes with entries from Meireki 3. The colophon reads, "Written in mid-winter of Meiji 25, Year of the Water Monkey, by Shuryo Sato." Below are the PDF files, provided with the permission of the Tanno family. Each is approximately 30MB. ・Togoku Taiheiki Vol. 1 ・Togoku Taiheiki Vol. 2 ・Togoku Taiheiki Vol. 3

Register of Family Genealogies of the Retainers of the Tome Date Clan

Record of Land Grants by Lord Harumune

Included in “A Study of the Date-ke Jinkatsu-shu”. It's quite an interesting historical source if you take a close look at it.

Fujiba Seisui-ki

A military chronicle of the Nikaido clan, lords of Sukagawa Castle. Included in the Battles section of Volume 22, Part 2 of the Zoku Gunsho Ruiju.

Bujo Kanjoki

A collection of military anecdotes. It was included after the Jozan Kidan.

Buhen Tokigaki

A collection of military anecdotes. It includes the origin of the bamboo-and-sparrow crest and Usami Nagamitsu's sword. It also covers the siege of Fukushima Castle from the Uesugi perspective. (Stories 109 and 110)

Masamune-ki

Written by Shigezane Date. A military chronicle spanning from Tensho 12 to Keicho 5. Included in Volume 11 of the Sendai Sosho. Also included in the Jinbutsu Orai-sha Sengoku Shiryo Sosho "Date Shiryoshu".

The Tale of Mogami Yoshimitsu

A military chronicle concerning Mogami Yoshimitsu. Included in the Battles section, Volume 22, Part 2 of the Zoku Gunsho Ruiju.

The Tale of Yamaguchi Dosai

A military chronicle of Yamaguchi Dosai, a retainer of the Hatakeyama clan of Nihonmatsu. Included in Volume 3 of the Sendai Sosho.

Yamanouchi Tenshoki

The Rise and Fall of the Yamanouchi Clan in Oku-Aizu. Includes Masamune's campaigns in Oku-Aizu. See “Oku-Aizu Sengoku Fudoki > Aizu Campaigns”.

Roo Kikigaki

Sendai Sosho Besshu, Vol. 3. Entries on the Katakura Family

Rojin Denbunki

Military accounts centered on Masamune. Included in Volume 6 of the Sendai Sosho.

Chronicle of the Waga Uprising

Included in the Battles section of Volume 22, Part 2 of the Zoku Gunsho Ruiju. A military chronicle from the Nanbu clan's perspective.

Watari Family Records

Chronicle of the Wakuya Date (Watari) clan. Included in Sendai Sosho, Vol. 9.

Brief Genealogy of the Watari Yoshin Family

A roster of retainers of the Watari Date clan, including their biographical histories.

Search by historical source name: Shiga Documents—Documents passed down through the Shiga family, senior retainers of the Watari Date clan. Warabi Shishido Family Documents—Documents passed down through the Shishido family, retainers of the Watari Date clan. Portions (?) have been transcribed in "Kyodo Watari No. 57."

About Sources and Conversion

This article is a Markdown conversion of the "Index of Date-Related Historical Materials by Name" from the Shigezane Date specialty site "Shigezane Zanmai" (administrator: TAKEMI Shigino), licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 2.1 Japan (CC BY-SA 2.1 JP). The original page can be found here: Index of Date-Related Historical Materials by Name (Shigezane Zanmai). Links within the text point directly to the original site pages as they were during the conversion process. Once corresponding articles are created on Neo Shigezane Zanmai, they will be redirected there accordingly.
